newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan power firms burn less oil, more coal in Nov.
newsitem.headline: Japan power firms burn less oil, more coal in Nov.

text.p: Electric utilities in Japan burned less crude and heavy fuel oil at their power plants in November than a year ago, while coal use rose 13 percent, the Federation of Electric Power Companies said on Tuesday.

Japan's 10 regional power firms consumed 1.18 million kilolitres (kl) of heavy fuel oil and 1.47 million kl of crude oil for thermal power production in November, down 11 percent and 0.3 percent, respectively, from the corresponding period a year ago.
Coal consumption, in contrast, rose 13.4 percent over the same period to 2.17 million tonnes.
Thermal power plants produced 35.3 billion kilowatt hour (kWh) of electricity in November, up 8.4 percent from a year earlier, the federation said.

Domestic heavy fuel oil demand for thermal power production fell 16.3 percent year-on-year in fiscal 1995/96 that ended in March, and was likely to drop 12.1 percent in the current fiscal year ending in March, the Institute of Energy Economics, a private research body, said earlier this month.
The institute also said that fuel oil demand from electric utilities was likely to fall another 8.7 percent in fiscal 1997/98 due to higher output at nuclear and hydropower plants.
